entries.when: Your best guess — you think it's likely (~70%+). たぶん雨だ (It's probably rain). Everyday default.
Opens a question or surprise — "Could it be that…?" もしかして彼？ (Could it be him?). You might be wrong.
Uncertainty on a statement — 雨かもしれない (It might rain). Attach to verb/adj; not a standalone question word.
Standalone pronoun — one thing near you. これは何？ (What is this?). Never put a noun after it.
Must sit before a noun — この本 (this book). For plural: この本たち ≈ "these books."
Standalone plural near you — これらは本 (These are books). Points at several items, not modifying a noun.
Standalone — near the listener or just mentioned. それください (Give me that).
Before a noun — その店 (that shop). Same ソ distance as それ.
Standalone plural — それらは古い (Those are old).
Near the speaker — where you are standing.
Near the listener — where they are or what you just pointed at.
Away from both of you — across the room or down the street.
Question word — どこ？ (Where?). Same こ/そ/あ/ど pattern.
Broad verb — listen, hear, or ask. 音楽を聞く (listen to music), 名前を聞く (ask a name). Default everyday "ask."
Deliberate inquiry — 道を尋ねる (ask for directions). More formal/focused; not for "listen to music."
Depart a place — ここを去る (leave here). Literary/formal feel; person or thing moves away.
Exit outward — 家を出る (leave the house), 出かける (go out). Physical "go out of" somewhere.
Leave something for someone — 荷物を残す (leave luggage behind). Object stays; you go.
Quit a job, school, or habit — 会社を辞める (quit the company). Not physical departure.
The rest, apart from what was mentioned — 他に何か？ (Anything else?). 他の人 (other people). Most common "other."
Emphasizes separation — 別の方法 (a different method), 別々に (separately). "Different" more than "the rest."
Catch-all for leftovers in lists — りんご、バナナ、その他 (apples, bananas, and others). Formal "etc."
Counting/addition — "one more." もう一つください (One more, please). Specific quantity, not "other" in general.
The action — to work. 会社で働く (work at a company). Verb: what you do.
The job itself — 仕事がある (I have work). Noun: the thing/place/task.
Polite default — bumping someone, getting attention, apologizing, or thanking for a favor.
Friends/family only — quick sorry. Stepped on a toe, late to meet up.
Casual-masculine sorry between close peers. Slightly weightier than ごめん.
Quantity or degree — もっと食べたい (want to eat more), もっと大きい (bigger). "More of" something.
Adding to a point — さらに問題がある (Furthermore, there's a problem). Formal "in addition" in speech/writing.
"Again" — また来て (Come again). Can mean "also" in lists, but primary sense is repetition.
Particle on a noun — 私も行く (I'm going too). "In addition" attached to the thing.
Hasn't happened yet — まだ食べてない (haven't eaten yet). Or "still" continuing.
Already done — もう食べた (already ate). With negative: もう行かない (not going anymore).
